scope: Verified byte-oriented MD5 against RFC 1321, SHA-256/384/512 against FIPS 180-4, AES-128/256 against FIPS 197-upd1, and CBC encryption/decryption against SP 800-38A section 6.2 and Appendices F.2.1/F.2.2/F.2.5/F.2.6. RC4 samples are checked against informational RFC 6229 section 2; this is vector evidence, not a normative cipher specification. The ISO 32000-2:2020 sponsored EC3 audit includes Algorithm 2.A SASLprep mapping, output, bidi and unassigned rules verified against RFC 4013 over RFC 3454 Unicode 3.2 tables, generated from the appendices and exhaustively compared with Python stringprep. Unicode 3.2.0 NFKC is implemented from the pinned bundled normalization data, with algorithmic Hangul, and checked against every NFKC relation in NormalizationTest-3.2.0.txt (16,992 rows; 84,960 relations). Complete SASLprep is independently checked with Python stringprep and unicodedata.ucd_3_2_0, including non-ASCII R6 user and owner authentication. RFC 3454 section 4 and its section 8.1 citation to UAX #15 revision 22 fix normalization to Unicode 3.2.0; only corrections present in that version apply. Other genuine qualifications remain: separately linked NIST examples are not locally supplied, R5 extension provenance is unverified, and the documented crypt-filter text conflicts, host-codepage conversion and document integration findings are outside this claim. No complete PDF conformance or side-channel certification is made.

requirements.gaps: The public APIs accept byte-aligned messages only. SHA-256 and SHA-384/512 are verified within the standard message-length ranges (less than 2^64 and 2^128 bits respectively); counter overflow wraps and is outside that claim. FIPS 180-4 Appendix A.2 points to separate worked digest examples, which are not available locally; existing digest values are independently corroborated with Python hashlib, not claimed as printed FIPS examples.
requirements.known_answer_coverage: All seven RFC 1321 Appendix A.5 messages rechecked; all 64 MD5 constants and shifts; all 144 SHA-2 constants and 24 initial words; the printed FIPS 180-4 abc padding examples; SHA-256/384/512 empty, abc, multi-block and million-a fixed digests, streaming splits, and independent Python hashlib boundary comparisons for byte lengths 0 through 261. Algorithm 2.B final SHA-256/384/512 branch vectors preserve full intermediate digests and select the leftmost 32 bytes only at the end.

clauses: FIPS 197-upd1 sections 3.4-3.5, 4.1-4.4, 5.1-5.3.4; Tables 3-6; Appendices A.1, A.3, B and C
SP 800-38A section 6.2 and Appendices F.2.1, F.2.2, F.2.5, F.2.6
RFC 6229 sections 1-2 (informational test vectors, not a cipher specification)
requirements.gaps: Separately linked FIPS 197-upd1 Appendix C examples are not locally supplied; older attributed block values remain corroborating tests. RFC 6229 provides informational RC4 test vectors rather than a normative cipher specification. AES-192 and a constant-time implementation are outside supported scope.
requirements.known_answer_coverage: All AES substitution entries; complete AES-128/256 Appendix A expansions; Appendix B output and 39 intermediate states; SP 800-38A F.2.1/F.2.2 and F.2.5/F.2.6 four-block encryption/decryption including intermediate blocks, fixed-ciphertext decryption and every block split. RFC 6229 section 2: both key families at 40/128/256 bits and every one of the 18 listed offsets, 108 samples total; all seven existing key-size initial samples and 40-bit offset samples rechecked. All 252 printed samples across fourteen keys were also independently compared with the Python encryptor when checking the source.

requirements.gaps: Document-layer dictionary and crypt-filter discrepancies are listed under integration_findings; Table 25 Length wording is internally inconsistent.

recovery_review.note: Literal EOL preservation, zero hash-padding removal and unsigned-P reinterpretation are reported repairs rather than normative parsing rules. No additional discrepancy was identified in that file; they are not marked verified standard behaviour.

corrected_oracles.crypto/r4-key7: The former successful-authentication expectation allowed an invalid 56-bit V=4 file key. Table 20 requires 128 bits, so this is now a syntax-rejection vector. R3 five- and seven-byte vectors continue to check the variable-length derivation math.

primitive_primary_texts.method: Read algorithm sections and Appendix A.5; numerical constants and counts checked against equations and the Rust implementation. No reference implementation was copied.
Read SHA-256/384/512 functions, constants, preprocessing and computation; compared all printed constants and initial words. The generator recomputes fractional roots using exact integer arithmetic.

Read finite-field definitions, cipher/inverse and expansion; compared every substitution entry and every supported Appendix A word. Numeric Appendix B examples are serialized by columns; prose is not redistributed.
Read section 6.2 and both supported four-block encryption/decryption examples; every numeric field was compared independently.
Read sections 1-2; checked every printed sample against the independent Python RC4 implementation, and added all offsets for both key families at the requested lengths.
Read preparation order and profile rules; parse numeric appendix ranges with the checked-in generator, then compare every membership across 0..10FFFF against Python stringprep.
Read sections 2.1-2.5 and examples in section 3; apply Unicode 3.2 mappings and validation without case folding. Normalization is an explicit unavailable-data boundary.

primitive_audit_steps.paraphrase: Append one bit, zeros to 448 mod 512, then the low 64 message-length bits in little-endian order.
primitive_audit_steps.implementation: Md5::finalize saves the original bit count, emits 0x80, pads across a block when needed, and appends little-endian length.
primitive_audit_steps.vectors: crypto/hash-padding-abc; crypto/hash-padding-boundaries (all lengths 0..261).

primitive_audit_steps.paraphrase: Parse words little-endian, initialize four specified words, and emit the accumulated state in little-endian order.
primitive_audit_steps.implementation: All four initial words and parsing/output conversions match.
primitive_audit_steps.vectors: rfc1321_suite checks all seven Appendix A.5 messages, including the multi-block message.

primitive_audit_steps.paraphrase: Apply the four Boolean functions and all 64 scheduled message words, sine constants and left rotations, then accumulate modulo 2^32.
primitive_audit_steps.implementation: Every constant and shift matches; each compact message-index expression was checked against the 64 listed operations, including state permutation and feed-forward.
primitive_audit_steps.vectors: crypto/md5-round-constants recomputes all sine constants independently; seven official digest answers and hashlib boundaries cover composition.

primitive_audit_steps.paraphrase: Use word-size-specific choice, majority, rotate/shift functions and the fractional cube-root round constants.
primitive_audit_steps.implementation: All Boolean expressions, rotation/shift counts, 64 32-bit constants and 80 64-bit constants match.
primitive_audit_steps.vectors: crypto/sha2-round-constants exact integer cube-root expectations; independent hashlib digest cases.

primitive_audit_steps.paraphrase: Pad to 448 or 896 bits per block, append 64- or 128-bit big-endian length and parse big-endian words.
primitive_audit_steps.implementation: The 56/112-byte thresholds, two-block padding paths, original bit counts and word conversions agree for byte-aligned messages within the standard length ranges.
primitive_audit_steps.vectors: crypto/hash-padding-abc reproduces both printed abc padding examples; digest comparison against hashlib; all boundary lengths and streaming splits.

primitive_audit_steps.paraphrase: Initialize SHA-256/512 from the first eight square roots and SHA-384 from prime roots nine through sixteen.
primitive_audit_steps.implementation: All 24 initial words match the printed values; SHA-384 has its own IV rather than a truncated SHA-512 IV.
primitive_audit_steps.vectors: crypto/sha2-round-constants independently derives every IV word with exact integer square roots.

primitive_audit_steps.paraphrase: Expand sixteen words to sixty-four with the small sigma recurrences, run the working-state rounds and add back the state.
primitive_audit_steps.implementation: Schedule offsets 2/7/15/16, sigma counts, T1/T2, variable movement and wrapping additions match.
primitive_audit_steps.vectors: hashlib_known_answers_and_streaming; crypto/hash-padding-boundaries and crypto/hash-padding-abc.

primitive_audit_steps.paraphrase: Use eighty 64-bit scheduled words and the 64-bit round functions with modular feed-forward.
primitive_audit_steps.implementation: Schedule bounds, offsets, rotations, T1/T2, working-state movement and wrapping additions match.
primitive_audit_steps.vectors: hashlib_known_answers_and_streaming; crypto/hash-padding-boundaries and crypto/hash-padding-abc.

primitive_audit_steps.paraphrase: Run the SHA-512 computation with the SHA-384 IV and retain the first six final words.
primitive_audit_steps.implementation: Sha384 uses sha64_compress with its own IV and serializes the leftmost 48 bytes.
primitive_audit_steps.vectors: Independent SHA-384 hashlib cases across both block boundaries, printed abc padding and all IV words.

primitive_audit_steps.locator: FIPS 180-4 Appendix A.2; FIPS 197-upd1 Appendix C
primitive_audit_steps.paraphrase: The local standards refer readers to separately published worked examples.

primitive_audit_steps.locator: SP 800-38A section 6.2; Appendices F.2.1, F.2.2, F.2.5, F.2.6
primitive_audit_steps.paraphrase: Before encrypting each block XOR its plaintext with the IV or prior ciphertext; decrypt each block then XOR with that same chaining value.
primitive_audit_steps.implementation: Both equations agree. In-place decryption saves each ciphertext block before overwriting it; the caller supplies the IV and whole blocks, with no implicit padding. Empty input is an API convenience returning empty output; no positive-block standard example is used to claim that extension. IV generation and unpredictability are the caller's responsibility, not provided by this primitive.
primitive_audit_steps.vectors: crypto/cbc-aes128-f2 and crypto/cbc-aes256-f2: all four encryption/decryption blocks and intermediate values, plus all block-boundary splits.

primitive_audit_steps.paraphrase: Compare independent RC4 implementations using two key families and samples at the document's listed keystream offsets.
primitive_audit_steps.implementation: Rust and independently authored Python KSA/PRGA agree with the printed samples. RFC 6229 does not specify the cipher and is not a normative RC4 algorithm certification.
primitive_audit_steps.vectors: crypto/rc4-rfc6229-{40,128,256}-key{1,2}: 18 sixteen-byte samples for each of six keys (108 samples); all existing initial-key values also rechecked.

timing_limitations.aes: Table-based: encryption, decryption and key expansion index forward/inverse S-box tables with secret-dependent values. GF multiplication also contains data-dependent branches; execution time and cache accesses can disclose information. No constant-time guarantee or side-channel resistance is claimed.
timing_limitations.context: The intended use is local document processing. A shared browser/process/hardware environment can still permit timing or cache observations. No algorithm rewrite or performance/security certification is implied by this audit.

saslprep_audit_steps.locator: RFC 4013 section 2.1; RFC 3454 Appendix B.1 and C.1.2
saslprep_audit_steps.paraphrase: Remove B.1 characters and replace other non-ASCII spaces with U+0020, without case folding.
saslprep_audit_steps.implementation: One range lookup per scalar; unchanged strings are borrowed. Mapping shrinks UTF-8 and uses checked allocation only when necessary.
saslprep_audit_steps.vectors: Every B.1/C.1.2 point in context, overlap and case preservation; four independently generated authenticated-key examples.

saslprep_audit_steps.locator: RFC 4013 section 2.2; RFC 3454 section 4; ISO 32000-2 7.6.4.3.3(a-b); RFC 3454 section 8.1 (UAX #15 revision 22, Unicode 3.2.0); bundled NormalizationTest-3.2.0.txt Parts 0-2
saslprep_audit_steps.paraphrase: Normalize the complete mapped string with Unicode 3.2 NFKC before output checks, UTF-8 encoding and byte truncation.
saslprep_audit_steps.implementation: nfkc32(input: Cow<str>) -> Result<Cow<str>> uses generated recursively expanded compatibility decompositions, stable counting sort by combining class, canonical pair composition with Full_Composition_Exclusion, and algorithmic Hangul. Quick-check Yes preserves ownership without allocation; scratch buffers grow fallibly. Static tables only; no runtime files or current-Unicode properties. Counting sort keeps arbitrary nonstarter runs linear.
saslprep_audit_steps.vectors: Every bundled conformance row: Part 0 = 23, Part 1 = 16,315, Part 2 = 654; no Part 3 is present in this version. All five columns normalize to column 4: 84,960 relations plus idempotence. Ten activated Python oracles and six correction/version cases agree.

saslprep_audit_steps.locator: RFC 4013 section 2.3; RFC 3454 section 5 and Appendices C.1.2, C.2.1, C.2.2, C.3-C.9
saslprep_audit_steps.paraphrase: Reject output containing any character selected by the profile's prohibition tables.
saslprep_audit_steps.implementation: Combined generated membership masks include every required C table. Rust str cannot contain surrogate scalars; malformed UTF-8 fails before preparation. Errors use Password and a byte position, never input text.
saslprep_audit_steps.vectors: Every table membership, prohibition range boundaries, ASCII controls including byte 127 and later, and malformed UTF-8. Validator tests are independent stages and need no normalization implementation. Also exercised after mapping and NFKC by the complete generated-password oracle.

saslprep_audit_steps.locator: RFC 4013 section 2.4; RFC 3454 section 6, Appendices D.1-D.2 and C.8
saslprep_audit_steps.paraphrase: When RandAL occurs, exclude LCat and require RandAL at both ends; prohibit the C.8 display-control set.
saslprep_audit_steps.implementation: Single pass accumulates the two directional classes and endpoint membership; C.8 is included in the prohibited mask. No Unicode version supplied by Rust is consulted.
saslprep_audit_steps.vectors: Pure RTL, RTL with internal digits, mixed RTL/Latin and invalid leading/trailing digits; all D.1/D.2 memberships compared with stringprep. Also exercised after mapping and NFKC by the complete generated-password oracle.

saslprep_audit_steps.locator: RFC 4013 section 2.5; RFC 3454 section 7 and Appendix A.1
saslprep_audit_steps.paraphrase: Stored strings exclude Unicode 3.2 unassigned code points; queries may also reject them.
saslprep_audit_steps.implementation: After complete Unicode 3.2 normalization, always reject A.1, applying the permitted stricter query policy to authentication as well.
saslprep_audit_steps.vectors: All A.1 memberships, U+0221 and code points assigned only in newer Unicode versions are checked against Python stringprep. Also exercised after mapping and NFKC by the complete generated-password oracle.

saslprep_audit_steps.locator: RFC 3454 Appendices A.1, B.1, C.1.2, C.2.1-C.9, D.1-D.2
saslprep_audit_steps.paraphrase: Use the appendix sets themselves, with Unicode 3.2 membership, rather than deriving them from prose or current Unicode categories.
saslprep_audit_steps.implementation: The Python generator parses only numeric code/range fields between explicit table markers, checks ordered ranges, compares all code points in all fourteen sets with stringprep, and emits merged Rust numeric ranges with symbolic membership flags and the pinned source SHA-256. Without the RFC, --check derives the same membership from stringprep alone.
saslprep_audit_steps.vectors: crypto/saslprep-table-membership is independently computed from Python predicates and compared against every generated Rust range and lookup gap.

saslprep_decisions.mapping_overlap: U+200B is in B.1 and C.1.2. B.1 removal takes precedence, matching the independent oracle; this explicit choice is not claimed as a separately ordered rule in RFC 4013.
saslprep_decisions.unassigned_policy: Use stored-string A.1 rejection for authentication queries too; RFC 3454 section 7 permits queries to reject unassigned code points.
saslprep_decisions.errors: Invalid UTF-8, prohibited output, unassigned output and bidi violations use Password, not document Syntax. Positions identify bytes in the relevant password buffer; fixed messages never embed password/key data.
saslprep_decisions.oracle: Python standard-library stringprep plus unicodedata.ucd_3_2_0 (Unicode 3.2.0) supplies independent complete-profile and normalization fixture expectations, never production normalization tables.
saslprep_decisions.normalization: The complete mapped string is normalized and validated before 127-byte truncation. Unicode 3.2 data is generated reproducibly by python3 tools/gen/unicode32.py; tools/check.py runs its --check. Production tables are generated only from bundled files, never from Python normalization.

normalization_corrections.source: RFC 3454 section 4 requires normalization of the profile Unicode version; section 8.1 explicitly cites UAX #15 version 3.2.0 revision 22 (tr15-22.html). The annex itself is not separately bundled; the pinned 3.2.0 normalization data, corrections and complete conformance corpus supply algorithm data and evidence.
normalization_corrections.decision: Apply F951 -> 964B from NormalizationCorrections-3.2.0.txt (introduced in 3.2.0 and already in UnicodeData). Do not apply corrections introduced after 3.2.0: retain 2F868 -> 2136A, 2F874 -> 5F33, 2F91F -> 43AB, 2F95F -> 7AAE and 2F9BF -> 4D57, as the bundled data and conformance rows require.
normalization_corrections.second_oracle: Python unicodedata.ucd_3_2_0 agrees on F951 and all five retained mappings; current unicodedata.normalize differs on the latter five and is deliberately not used.
normalization_corrections.generator_check: The generator validates correction version and corrected decomposition, and checks Full_Composition_Exclusion against explicit exclusions plus canonical singletons and nonstarter decompositions.

saslprep_decisions.unicode_notice: Generated normalization source embeds the complete Unicode License V3 copyright and permission notice. pagura_crypto::unicode_notice() includes data/unicode/LICENSE for licence-listing callers.

normalization_evidence.part_3: Absent from the bundled Unicode 3.2.0 file, not skipped.
normalization_evidence.size_method: Same locked offline release build of pagura-host for wasm32-wasip1 before and after this implementation. The whole-file increase includes normalizer code as well as tables; 68,967 is the separate static table payload computed using Rust size_of_val and the UTF-8 pool length. No performance certification.
